question: Should TL100 train its tokenizer or borrow a pretrained vocabulary?

options_considered.summary: Implement and train a readable byte-level BPE tokenizer on the approved TL100 corpus.
advantages: The vocabulary and every merge are inspectable.

options_considered.summary: Use an existing pretrained tokenizer and vocabulary.
disadvantages: The vocabulary imports an opaque acquisition history.
It weakens the glass-box learning objective.

recommendation: Build a byte-level BPE tokenizer and retain byte-only encoding as the transparent baseline.
pedagogical_value: Exposes the mapping from UTF-8 bytes to learned lexical units and its model-cost consequences.
risks: A tokenizer trained on too little pilot text may learn brittle merges.
failure_tests: Require agreement with an independently structured encoder.
owner_decision: Build the tokenizer in-project; keep the development tokenizer provisional until the pilot bakeoff.
